note: Machine-readable registry of what is actually unsolved in this repo. Add an entry the moment something is found open; do not let it live only in prose. `kind` says what class of evidence would settle it, not how hard it is.

kinds.CODE: settled by a runnable implementation plus a falsifier
kinds.DERIVATION: settled by an argument from stated premises, checkable by computation
kinds.DEFINITION: settled by choosing and defending a definition; the gap is conceptual, not computational
kinds.BENCH: settled only by an instrument reading. Cost and instrument are named.

problems.title: What the physical anchor standard IS
problems.statement: The INSTRUMENT route asks whether a stability reference moved at the same timestamp as a residual. The mechanism is built: anchor_dev is a declared deviation against an explicit ANCHOR_TOL. What is not specified is the reference itself.
problems.why_open: It needs a standard whose failure mode does not correlate with the working sensors'. An anchor that drifts the same way as the sensor it checks is not an anchor.
would_count: A named physical reference per channel whose value is set by something other than the sensor electronics
An Allan-deviation curve for that reference, at rest, giving ANCHOR_TOL as a function of averaging time
A stated failure mode, and an argument that it is uncorrelated with the working sensor's

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: for a float sensor that means 'any nonzero', which is always true

leads: Allan variance (Allan 1966; IEEE Std 952) separates white / flicker / random-walk drift by log-log slope
Dissimilar redundancy: sensors of different physical principle, so failure modes do not correlate
Analytical redundancy / parity space (Chow & Willsky 1984) needs no reference standard at all, only redundancy plus a model
Thermodynamically-fixed anchors: ice bath, saturated salt slurries (ASTM E104: LiCl 11.3% RH, MgCl2 33%, NaCl 75%), calibration mass, shorted/open input, Spectralon reflectance target
Westgard multi-rule QC has published error-detection and false-rejection rates per rule

problems.title: The conservation ledger: what is the reservoir, in what units
problems.statement: The spend ledger counts query cost and credits whether the funded query moved a claim. That is a budget with a yield, not a conservation law. Without a reservoir there is no way to state that the loop is not creating information from nothing.
problems.why_open: Units were never stated, so they were not guessed. Three candidate reservoirs exist and they are not the same quantity.
would_count: A named conserved quantity with units
A measurement procedure for it from the existing logs
A demonstration that the loop cannot increase it without an input
leads: Expected information gain (Lindley 1956), in bits or nats: KL from prior to posterior
Value of information (Howard 1966), units of whatever the decision pays in
Stochastic thermodynamics: Sagawa-Ueda; Parrondo, Horowitz & Sagawa 2015. Continuous with the Landauer work already in Negentropic/
Empowerment (Klyubin, Polani & Nehaniv 2005): channel capacity actuators -> sensors, in bits

problems.title: What a shape-level claim band IS
problems.statement: shape is documented canonical -- 'Do NOT scalarize on ingest' -- and no code path reads it. test() compares value only, so every claim in the system is a claim about one scalar projection.
problems.why_open: Storing the shape without testing against it is scalarizing with a receipt. A reading carrying a shape must now name its projection, which makes the loss explicit and auditable, but does not remove it. What a band on a vector, a spectrum, or a multi-axis reading should BE is a physics question.
would_count: A definition of 'inside the band' for a non-scalar reading that is not a norm in disguise
A signed residual for it, so the correlation branch still has something to correlate
A demonstration on a real multi-axis reading where the shape-level test and the scalar test disagree, and an argument for which is right

problems.title: Period estimation, and the scanned lag range
problems.statement: The slotted autocorrelation reports STRUCTURED with a calibrated p-value but refuses to name a period, because the argmax lag is not one: a rider peaks at every multiple of T/2 and noise picks the winner. Separately, a rider whose period exceeds n_slots*slot_width is invisible; lag_range_s is reported but nothing widens it.
problems.why_open: Both textbook autocorrelation handles were measured and both refused. Smallest-significant is always slot 1 because rho -> 1 as tau -> 0. First-local-minimum ran biased low and worsened with period: 7.5 s against a true 10.0.
would_count: A period estimate on irregularly sampled data with measured error against known riders
A false-alarm rate on white noise at a stated alpha
Stdlib only, no numpy

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: median 8.8 s against a true T/2 of 3.0 s on a Poisson clock
biased low, worsening with period: 7.5 s against a true 10.0 at T=20

leads: Lomb-Scargle (Lomb 1976; Scargle 1982); floating-mean generalisation (Zechmeister & Kuerster 2009)
CLEAN deconvolution of the spectral window (Roberts, Lehar & Dreher 1987)

problems.title: The exact binomial tail is discrete, and the conservatism costs power
problems.statement: The covariate gate uses an exact one-sided binomial tail. Because the distribution is discrete, the achieved level sits near 1% against a nominal 5%. That conservatism costs more power than the choice between Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg does.
problems.why_open: Measured but not fixed. Recovering the level is a known problem with known answers, none of which were implemented.
would_count: A gate whose achieved false-positive rate is close to the nominal alpha on the same nulls
Measured power gain against the current gate on the same real effect
No increase in false-positive rate
leads: mid-p correction
randomised / fuzzy decision at the boundary
Berger-Boos or similar

problems.title: MISSING_VARIABLE is correlational and cannot conclude
problems.statement: The branch tests whether residuals concentrate under a covariate. It is now correctly calibrated, and it still cannot distinguish a cause from a confounder.
problems.why_open: 'Concentrates under' is not 'is caused by'. With enough logged covariates something always concentrates, which the calibration fixes; it does not fix the inferential gap.
would_count: A conditional-independence test over the logged covariates, stdlib
A worked case where the marginal and conditional verdicts differ
An honest statement of what the loop can and cannot conclude from observational logging alone
leads: Peters, Janzing & Schoelkopf, Elements of Causal Inference (free online)
Simpson's paradox as the concrete failure

problems.title: Trajectory-level entropy production
problems.statement: Negentropic/ entropy production is a housekeeping estimator with a known sign bias. NEG-8 (persistence margin Phi = -S_exchange - sigma) cannot be evaluated on simulated traces until sigma is estimated at trajectory level.
would_count: A MaxCal or equivalent trajectory-level estimator
Sign-bias measured against a known-sigma simulation
Stdlib tier

problems.title: Two falsifiers implemented and never run against data
problems.statement: NEG-2 (archive lifetime under an expanding maintenance schedule) and NEG-3 (finite-time Landauer erasure, tau^-1 excess scaling) have runnable falsifiers and no data.
would_count: A dataset, its provenance, and the falsifier's verdict on it

problems.title: Derive the merit weights from something, or call it a mean
problems.statement: The five sovereignty criteria ship at 0.20 each. 77% of random reweightings reproduce the same high-merit rate, so the weights carry no information. evaluate_pattern now reports weights_are_flat alongside every score.
would_count: Weights derived from a stated procedure, not asserted
verdict_is_weight_sensitive() returning weights_carry_information = True on real patterns
Or: an argument that an unweighted mean is correct, in which case rename total_score

problems.title: Measure logical consistency instead of naming it unmeasured
problems.statement: _check_internal_coherence carried a flat 0.4 placeholder for logical consistency. The term was removed rather than guessed at, and logical_consistency is now listed in unmeasured_components.
would_count: A computable check over Pattern.mathematical_structure
Its own weight, stated
A pair of patterns it separates that the current two components do not

problems.title: Energy per bit has three values and they differ in legality
problems.statement: 1-2 aJ is 348 kT ln2 (legal). 0.1 eV is 5.6 kT ln2 (legal). 0.01 eV is 0.56 kT ln2, below the Landauer bound at 300 K.
problems.why_open: Pick one and propagate it through the documents that depend on it. 0.01 eV cannot be it.
would_count: One value, chosen with a stated basis
Every downstream figure recomputed
reach(E, 'landauer 300K') returning DETECTABLE

problems.title: Are 8 implant states separable at >3 sigma?
problems.statement: Eight doping states, measured as (sheet resistance, carrier type, carrier concentration). Separable at >3 sigma or not.
problems.why_open: Cheap, decisive, unrun. Needs no magnet, no cryostat, no THz source.
would_count: Measured (R_s, type, n) for 8 states with error bars
Pairwise separation in sigma
Cost and instrument named

problems.title: Piezoresistive dR/R at 0.1% strain
problems.statement: The strain channel that replaces every magnetic proposal predicts dR/R about 9% at 0.1% strain, gauge factor about 121 for pi_l along <110> paired with E<110> = 169 GPa.
problems.why_open: A strain gauge and a four-point probe settle it. Unrun.
would_count: Measured dR/R vs strain
Extracted gauge factor with the crystal direction stated
Agreement or disagreement with 121

problems.title: Bifilar common-mode rejection at achievable matching tolerance
problems.statement: The 60 dB common-mode suppression budget depends on a matching tolerance that was assumed, not measured.
would_count: Measured CMRR by magneto-optic sampling at a stated frequency
The matching tolerance actually achieved
Comparison against the budget in transient_suppression.py

problems.title: An n-dependent bit width against a fixed-width encoder contract
problems.statement: Negentropic/emit_ising.py does not inherit from bridges/abstract_encoder.py. The blocker is that an Ising spec has a bit width that depends on n, while every other encoder emits a fixed width.
would_count: A contract that admits both, or an argument that they are different kinds of thing and should not share one

problems.title: The Raman photon budget on the actual rig
problems.statement: The proposed architecture assumes a 1024-point spectrum on every acquisition, with a scheduler budgeting model frames per acquisition, for live imaging. A shot-noise budget at 785 nm / 10 mW / NA 1.2 / 25% throughput gives 30-300 s per spectrum at SNR 10 per channel, so the acquisition is the bottleneck by one to two orders and the scheduler is optimising the wrong resource.
problems.why_open: The estimate uses assumed cross-sections and scatterer densities. The rig's own number settles it and nothing else does.
would_count: Photons per channel per second measured on one unperturbed cell at the working power
The resulting seconds-per-spectrum at a stated SNR
The achievable frames per hour, which fixes n for every downstream model
leads: repo_guard.reach is the same comparison, already mechanised
Coherent Raman (SRS/CARS) buys 1e4-1e5 but is narrowband: sweeping 1024 points gives the time back
Broadband CARS buys ~1e2-1e3 against a worse nonresonant background

problems.title: False-alarm rate of a latent-space claim predicate
problems.statement: The example claim is `u[0] > 0.5 and u[1] < -0.2` with falsification after 3 consecutive failures. Nothing states the per-observation false-alarm rate on an unperturbed cell, so the stopping rule has no calibration.
problems.why_open: FCL-5 is the same shape: `rate > 1.5 x base` fired on 34-41% of null sets while its own notes said only 'too permissive'.
would_count: Technical replicates of one unperturbed cell
The predicate run against them, with the false-alarm count
A threshold set from that number rather than from inspection

problems.title: Does the manifold separate biochemistry, or batch structure?
problems.statement: 'The manifold learns to distinguish cell states.' Untested against a null in which the biochemistry is destroyed and the acquisition structure is kept.
would_count: The identical architecture trained on phase-randomised spectra, or on real spectra with shuffled state labels
Separation measured the same way in both
A stated margin between them
leads: repo_guard.null_harness
NEG-7 died exactly here

problems.title: A claim that survives retraining the encoder
problems.statement: A hypothesis written as `u[1] > 0.3` is a claim about one fitting run: retrain the encoder and the axes rotate. The latent is also learned from the same spectra the claim is tested on.
problems.why_open: This is P-SELF-SUPPLIED-FALSIFIER, the largest unmechanised shape in PRINCIPLES.json.
would_count: Claims stated in spectral terms -- a band, a ratio, a shift -- rather than latent coordinates
Or: a frozen encoder, a held-out split, and the claim written before the split is seen
A demonstration that the claim's verdict is unchanged across two independent training runs

problems.title: Full spectrum at minutes, or a few bands at video rate
problems.statement: The design assumes both a 1024-point spectrum and real-time acquisition. Spontaneous Raman gives the first; coherent Raman gives the second for one or a few shifts. No instrument gives both.
would_count: A stated choice, with the model redesigned for the n it implies
Or a named instrument that delivers both, with its throughput

problems.title: What BLOCKAGE's condition should be
problems.statement: BLOCKAGE is 'flow obstruction, resistance' and its rule -- pressure high while total magnitude low -- is unsatisfiable because pressure is one of the magnitudes summed. The intent is legible; the predicate is not.
problems.why_open: Replacing it means deciding what 'low flow' is measured against, and nothing in the sensor suite currently reports a flow. Picking a threshold here would be inventing an affect model, which is not this repo's to write.
would_count: A predicate over quantities the SensorSuite actually reports, which is satisfiable by at least one reading set
A statement of what BLOCKAGE is meant to distinguish FROM -- most plausibly RE_NORMALIZE and HEAT_FLUX, which both already fire on pressure
The reading sets that should and should not produce it, supplied independently of the predicate

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: pressure is a term of total_magnitude over non-negative values, so the conjunction is empty

problems.title: The rule ladder's precedence
problems.statement: Glyph.from_sensor_state tests twelve rules top to bottom and returns the first match, so an earlier rule shadows every later one it overlaps. Measured: the HEAT_FLUX exemplar satisfies RE_NORMALIZE's rule, which is tested first, and four more glyphs fall to a trailing 'RESONANCE if anything is active' default.
problems.why_open: The overlaps are real -- discordance, fatigue and pressure appear in several rules -- so the fix is either a declared precedence or a scored match rather than a first match. Both are affect-model decisions.
would_count: A stated precedence with a reason per pair, or a scoring rule that makes precedence unnecessary
Recovery from the phase_space specification above 7/12 without weakening any individual rule
A demonstration that no glyph becomes unreachable in the process -- unreachable_glyphs() must still return only what arithmetic forbids
leads: A conjunction ladder with overlapping antecedents is a decision list; ordering one to maximise agreement with labelled data is the standard formulation and needs labels
Scoring every rule and taking the argmax removes precedence but introduces a tie policy

problems.title: Whether the decay and energy layer should be carried forward
problems.statement: The superseded half carried DecayModel, per-glyph energy_cost, velocity, relax() and an energy budget. None of it was ported, because it attached to a classifier that recovered 4 of 12 and because the energy figures are per-glyph constants with nothing behind them.
problems.why_open: Porting it would carry the classification error into a thermodynamic accounting layer, where a wrong glyph becomes a wrong energy. Whether the layer is worth having at all depends on what the energies are supposed to be measurements OF, which is unstated.
would_count: A statement of what energy_cost has units of, and what physical or informational quantity it tracks
Any measurement that could contradict a specific glyph's energy_cost
A decay model tested against a time series rather than asserted per glyph

prior_attempts.what: twelve hand-assigned energy_cost constants from 0.0 to 0.9
prior_attempts.why_it_failed: nothing in the file or its tests could have disagreed with any of them

leads: Negentropic/landauer.py already carries the one energy bound that is not negotiable, if these are informational costs
Negentropic/persistence.py's margin is dimensionally explicit, which M(S) was not -- the same trap

problems.title: Make scale an input from the experiment, not an inference
problems.statement: NonLocalCorrelationSensor.update infers scale from correlation_strength when the caller omits it, after which scale/technique agreement is vacuous (0 mismatches over 21 strengths) and a strong cross-system correlation is recorded as cellular.
problems.why_open: The non-circular path already exists -- pass scale= -- and nothing calls it that way. Removing the fallback is an interface change with callers this repo cannot see, and the alternative of defaulting scale to None means deciding what the sensor reports when the experiment did not say.
would_count: Every call site supplying scale from the sampling design: extent, interval, what was sampled
A decision on what update() does when scale is genuinely unknown -- refuse, or record None and let downstream handle it
pairing_is_tautological() returning mismatches > 0 on real data, which is only possible once the two sides have independent sources

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: correlation strength is a property of the result and scale is a property of the experiment; no mechanism relates them, and the map excludes the target observation

leads: The AISS remedy: report the degeneracy beside the answer rather than invent a disagreement -- done, as scale_is_inferred
The spec itself lives in the Emotions-as-Sensors repo and is not mounted here; its scale vocabulary may not be these four names

problems.title: What audit() computes
problems.statement: What audit() and correct() compute. ANSWERED by a second drop containing core.py; both are implemented.
problems.why_open: Closed. The answers were: audit() enumerates simple cycles by DFS, composes each into an affine map, and scores it as the deviation from identity AT x = 1; correct() nudges every edge in every inconsistent cycle by a phi^-9-scaled step. Both turned out to carry defects a reconstruction would not have reproduced -- GI-11 and GI-13 -- which is why refusing to guess was the right call. The two questions that remain are GI-11a and GI-13a.
would_count: Closed by arrival of the file, not by argument.

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: not a failure -- it is the current state, on the same principle as Silicon/fp4_autopilot.py's ber_sweep()

leads: A cycle basis of a directed graph has V-E+C independent cycles; scoring all simple cycles double-counts
For pure-scale edges the log of the product is additive, which turns cycle consistency into a least-squares problem on log values
GI-3 is the reason this matters: two routes disagreeing is the finding, and check() currently hides it

problems.title: One ledger, and a claim that can decline to be written
problems.statement: bridge.py arrived and works. What is unresolved is the ledger it writes to and what it does when it has nothing to say: LEDGER is a relative path at 24 sites across bridge.py and fabrication/, with no locking, and an acyclic network writes an integrity claim of 0.0 that verify_edge_measurement then divides by.
problems.why_open: Three decisions, none of them coding questions. Where the ledger lives (an absolute path anchored to the repo root, or JSONL so concurrent appends are safe). What a claim record does when the quantity is undefined -- decline to write, or carry an explicit no-evidence state, because a 0.0 in a ledger cannot be told from a failure. And whether a relative error is the right verdict for every claim type, since it is undefined at zero for all of them.
would_count: All 24 LEDGER sites moved together, or a stated reason to keep them split
A no-evidence state in the record, distinct from a zero value
A verdict rule for claims whose predicted value is legitimately zero -- a rotate edge at angle 0 is the worked case
Concurrent-append behaviour stated and tested

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: relative to the working directory, so the ledger written depends on where the tool was run
honest as an answer, unreadable as a record -- and it is the value GB-1 divides by

leads: fabrication/emit/_common.py shows the payload shape and the dedupe-by-scope pattern
GI-1 means a claim about a node value would be checked against a prediction that ignores measurements

problems.title: Whether phi is doing any work in the resonance thresholds
problems.statement: resonance.py gates on PHI_INV_9 * 10 = 0.1316 for band anomalies and 1 + PHI_INV_9 * 100 = 2.3156 for injections. In both the multiplier sets the scale and the phi constant contributes a factor between 1 and 2.
problems.why_open: A constant multiplied by a round number until it looks right is a chosen number wearing a derivation. Either phi^-9 follows from something about phi-ratio bands -- in which case the multiplier needs the same treatment -- or the thresholds are empirical and should say so and be calibrated like any other threshold.
would_count: A derivation of 0.1316 and 2.3156 from the band structure, or
A measured false-alarm and detection rate at each, against a null, which makes them empirical and honest
Either way, a statement of which of the two they are

prior_attempts.what: phi^-9 as the residual tolerance in integrity.py
prior_attempts.why_it_failed: not failed -- there it is used directly at 1.3 % with no multiplier, which is the consistent case

problems.title: A closure test that is not a single probe
problems.statement: find_cycles composes each cycle into an affine map x -> a*x + b and scores it as abs(a*1 + b - 1), so every map with a + b = 1 passes. The two numbers that determine the map are already computed and one of them is discarded.
problems.why_open: The replacement is nearly free -- compare (a, b) to (1, 0) -- but it changes what closure_error MEANS, and closure_error is written into ledger claims with tol_frac = phi^-9. A two-component residual needs a combination rule, and picking one silently rescales every existing cycle claim.
would_count: A residual over both components with a stated combination rule
A demonstration that pure-scale cycles keep their current values, so existing ledger entries do not all move
The compose(2, -1) cycle failing, and a genuine identity cycle passing
leads: abs(a-1) + abs(b) and hypot(a-1, b) differ only in the mixed case; the first is scale-free in b, the second is not
Evaluating at two points is equivalent and needs no rule, but the choice of points is then the free parameter

problems.title: What correct() is allowed to move
problems.statement: correct() distributes a cycle's closure error across every edge in the cycle. Measured on the drop's own defect: an edge 23.6% high converges to +11.9% with its inverse partner at -9.5%, and audit() then reports every cycle consistent.
problems.why_open: Reaching self-consistency by moving everything is always possible and tells you nothing. Restoring the RIGHT value needs a reference the network does not contain. So the question is which edges are held fixed -- and that is a statement about what is known, not about the algorithm.
would_count: A way to mark an edge as trusted, so correction cannot move it
A report of WHAT was moved and by how much, not just a count of adjustments
A stated stopping rule; the current step is phi^-9 * residual / len(cycle), which at max_iter=5 moves nothing measurable and at 500 converges to a wrong value

prior_attempts.what: uniform phi^-9-scaled nudges across every edge of every bad cycle
prior_attempts.why_it_failed: the error is split between the wrong edge and its inverse partner until the product closes; the defect is hidden, not removed

leads: Least squares on log factors with a fixed subset is the standard form for pure-scale networks, and has a unique solution
GI-1 is the other half: the measurements are the external reference, and nothing currently feeds them into correction

problems.title: What integrity_score is a score of
problems.statement: core.audit() returns base_score * (1 + mean_edge_weight); integrity.full_report() returns coverage * (trusted/measured). Both are called integrity_score, both are compared to INTEGRITY_THRESHOLD = 3.618, their ranges are [0, 2] and [0, 1], and neither reaches it.
problems.why_open: Multiplying a consistency fraction by an author-declared confidence gives a number with the units of neither, and the (1 + w) form means declaring no confidence costs nothing. Separating them is easy; deciding what a caller should gate on is not, and that decision is what the threshold was standing in for.
would_count: The two factors reported separately, with the threshold attached to whichever one it is about
A name for each of the two quantities that does not collide
A stated range for `weight`, since the score's ceiling depends on it
leads: GI-2 and GI-12 are the same constant seen from two modules
AISS's flat merit weights are the nearest prior: an unweighted mean wearing a weighting

problems.title: A stiffness-temperature correction with the right term
problems.statement: fabrication/temperature.py's k_correct builds a stiffness correction from thermal expansion alone, on the stated reasoning that 'E changes slightly with temperature; dominant effect is length'. For steel the two coefficients are alpha = 12e-6/C and dE/E ~ -2.4e-4/C, so the reasoning is inverted and the correction is ~20x too small with the wrong sign.
problems.why_open: Writing dE/E in is a line of code. What is missing is the coefficient per material, and a statement of what mode the resonance IS -- a cantilever, a plate and a Helmholtz cavity scale differently with E and with dimension, and normalize_measurement currently applies one formula to 'mechanical / resonance_freq_Hz' whatever the geometry.
would_count: A dE/dT table alongside the existing ALPHA table, with sources
A mode factor, or a refusal to correct when the mode is unstated
A bench check that can see it: 0.024% is invisible against +/-8%, so the test has to be a coefficient comparison, not a measurement

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: the modulus term is 20x larger and opposite in sign; the correction is invisible in any test narrow enough to run

leads: Steel E drops ~2-3e-4 per C over -50..+200 C; aluminium ~5e-4
f ~ sqrt(E) for most flexural modes, so df/f = 0.5 dE/E

problems.title: One reference temperature
problems.statement: fabrication/temperature.py has five functions defaulting ref_temp_c to 20 C and three to 15 C, and normalize_measurement passes its 15 C into r_correct, whose TCR is the copper value specified at 20 C -- a 2.0% bias on every electrical normalisation at the default.
problems.why_open: Picking one is a two-line change; picking WHICH is not. 15 C is the acoustic convention baked into C_AIR = 343.0 and every existing acoustic claim in the ledger; 20 C is the convention every component tempco is specified at. Moving either re-bases claims already recorded.
would_count: A single module-level REF_TEMP_C with a stated reason
A pass over existing ledger claims saying which were made at which reference, or a statement that none were
Each tempco carrying the temperature it is specified at, so a mismatch is detectable rather than silent

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: they cross inside normalize_measurement and nothing reports the crossing

problems.title: A two-sided drift detector
problems.statement: trend.py computes fail_threshold as predicted*(1 + 2*tol_frac) -- an upper edge only. A value drifting DOWN out of its band is never classified failed, and when a value is already above the threshold and falling, predicted_fail_days reports the time to come back inside.
problems.why_open: The repair is one band and one sign convention, and it is held only by needing to decide what 'time to failure' means for a value already outside: time to the far edge, or nothing at all. Both are defensible and they read very differently in a report.
would_count: Both edges, with the crossing timed against whichever the slope approaches
A stated answer for an already-failed value
The measured cases passing: a 10.0-ohm claim fallen to 0.5 reports failed, and a value falling from 30.0 toward a 10.0 claim does not report a fail date

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: one edge; and the negative branch answers a different question in a field named for this one

problems.title: Calibrating the trend verdicts
problems.statement: trend.py classifies on r2 > 0.5 and r2 > 0.7 with no minimum sample count, so two points give R^2 = 1.0 by construction and always read as a trend; and the stable gate abs(slope) < 1e-6 is an absolute number compared against ohms, hertz and kelvin per day alike.
problems.why_open: Both thresholds need what FCL-5/6 needed: a null. Feed the detector sequences with no drift and count how often each verdict fires, at each sample count. Nobody has run that, and until it is run the verdicts are labels rather than rates.
would_count: A false-alarm rate per verdict against a no-drift null, as a function of n
A minimum sample count derived from it, rather than chosen
A relative slope gate, so the stable verdict compares across domains
Power: the drift the detector reliably catches at n = 10, 20, 50

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: neither has been run against data where the answer is known to be no

leads: The exact binomial tail and BH correction from field/field_claim_loop.py apply directly once the pairs are counted
R^2 has a known null distribution for a line through n iid points

problems.title: Cross-domain correlation that is not a statement about time
problems.statement: cross_domain_correlation gates on |r| > 0.6 with no null. Two monotone drifts correlate at ~1 whatever their cause -- measured at exactly 1.0000 between the fixture's thermal and mechanical ramps. Separately the overlap is an exact float-timestamp intersection, so a millisecond of jitter drops it to zero, and the defaults compare electrical against thermal, which is the one pair in the fixture that does not correlate.
problems.why_open: Detrending is the standard first move and it changes what the function answers -- from 'do these move together' to 'do their residuals move together', which is the interesting question and a different one. Timestamp binning needs a tolerance nobody has stated.
would_count: Residual correlation after removing each series' own trend
A permutation null, and a correction over the pairs tested
Timestamp binning at a stated tolerance
All domain pairs iterated, not a default pair
The thermal x mechanical pair in the fixture reporting NO residual correlation, since both are noiseless ramps

prior_attempts.what: Pearson r on raw series, |r| > 0.6, exact timestamp match
prior_attempts.why_it_failed: r = 1.0000 on two unrelated ramps; and returns nothing at all on any real log

problems.title: A claim about a response, not a threshold at one point
problems.statement: Every claim in adaptive_sim is a threshold on a single run. The framework generates claims of the form 'X is correlated with parameter P' -- one shipped, describing a correlation between power-law slope and seed injection rate -- and then tests them by comparing X to a constant on one run in which P was never varied. So the stated content and the executed test are different claims.
problems.why_open: It needs a second loop shape. The existing loop varies parameters to CHASE a threshold, adapting until a claim passes; a response claim needs a sweep with the claim held fixed, and fitting across runs afterwards. Merging the two naively gives a loop that adapts its way to whatever correlation it was looking for, which is the shape that manufactures a fit rather than measuring one.
would_count: A sweep runner that holds every claim fixed while varying one parameter over a stated grid
The fit reported with a null: shuffle the parameter against the outcomes and report where the observed slope sits
A refusal to emit a response claim from fewer than a stated number of distinct parameter values
The adaptive loop and the sweep kept separable, so a sweep cannot be run on parameters the agent has been steering

prior_attempts.what: Emitting the claim from a single run with a threshold on the outcome
prior_attempts.why_it_failed: ASF-15. The description asserts a correlation, the test is `slope < -1.5` at one point, and seed_rate is never varied. It also fails on arrival, being written in the density-exponent convention while the tested quantity is a binned-count slope (ASF-9).

problems.title: A precondition for testing a distributional claim at all
problems.statement: mortality_base 0.2 empties the forest grid, and the only symptom is claims returning inconclusive one at a time. A run with no trees, or with too few for a 30-bin histogram, is a failed experiment rather than a source of weak evidence, and nothing marks it as one.
problems.why_open: The floor is a number and the number is a claim. `len(sizes) > 100` is already in the fitting code as an unexplained constant, and the right value depends on the bin count and on what the fit is for -- the literature's answer for power-law fitting is not a count threshold at all.
would_count: A stated precondition on the run, evaluated before any distributional claim is tested
The threshold derived from the bin count and occupancy rather than asserted
A degenerate run reported as degenerate once, not as N separate inconclusive claims

prior_attempts.what: `if len(sizes) > 100` inside the fitting function, and `np.sum(mask) > 5` on occupied bins
prior_attempts.why_it_failed: Both are unexplained constants that silently return None, so the caller sees a missing key rather than a stated precondition. Six occupied bins is enough for R2 > 0.6 on almost anything.

problems.title: Null-harness the forest model, not only its fitting code
problems.statement: ASF-8 nulls the FITTING code against distributions with known answers, which is what made the R2 gate's blindness visible. It does not null the MODEL. What size distribution does this grid produce when metabolic scaling is replaced by a constant growth rate, or when competition is switched off entirely (which ASF-12 shows is one parameter value away)? If R2 > 0.6 survives those substitutions, the claim is measuring the binning and the grid geometry rather than the biology.
problems.why_open: Not run. It is repo_guard's null-harness stage applied to a model rather than to a statistic, and the substitution has to preserve the thing that is not under test -- same grid, same mortality, same seed rain -- which takes a stated null model rather than a switch.
would_count: A constant-growth null with everything else held fixed, and the R2 distribution under it
A no-competition null (competition_radius 0, which ASF-12 makes reachable and explicit)
The observed R2 reported as a position in the null distribution rather than against 0.6
A statement of which substitution the claim is supposed to survive, written before the numbers

leads.what: ASF-12 already exposes competition_radius, so the no-competition null needs no new code path
